verse: Let us examine and test our ways, and turn back to the LORD.
story: In the middle of his grief over a ruined Jerusalem, the poet stops speaking only for himself and turns to the people beside him.

Until now the chapter has been one man's lament, but here the voice becomes plural: let us. He has just remembered that the LORD's mercies are new every morning, and that memory gives him the courage to look honestly at sin. He does not ask God to inspect them from a distance. He calls them to search their own ways, to name what they find, and then to come home. Repentance here is not despair; it is the road back to a God whose loving devotion has not run out.
Lent invites the same slow, honest look. Whatever you find today, you are not turning toward a closed door but toward the LORD who is waiting.
theme: Lent: repentance, the road to the cross
